decisions.context: Authorization needs a fraud score before it proceeds, and scores must return within tens of milliseconds. An asynchronous scoring path would not meet that sequence.

alternatives.label: Synchronous scoring request
pros: Low latency: score available in authorization path
cons: Peak availability: scoring delays can delay authorization

alternatives.label: Asynchronous scoring queue
cons: Score before authorization: result may arrive too late

decisions.rationale: Scoring before authorization decides the choice. This gives up the queue's ability to absorb bursts, so the synchronous path must be sized and managed for peak traffic.
consequences: Authorization depends on the scoring path's response time.
The scoring service needs capacity for peak request rates.

decisions.context: The service must keep working during transaction peaks while meeting a tight response-time target. Multiple serving instances can add capacity and reduce reliance on a single instance.

alternatives.label: Horizontally scaled serving instances
pros: Peak availability: capacity can be distributed across instances
Low latency: concurrent requests handled in parallel
cons: Peak availability: instance coordination adds operational complexity

alternatives.label: Single larger serving instance
cons: Peak availability: one instance limits capacity and creates a failure point

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: distributing serving capacity avoids depending on one instance. The trade-off is more deployment and coordination complexity.
consequences: The service must distribute requests across instances.
Capacity management must account for peak demand.

decisions.decision: Record model and feature provenance with each score
decisions.context: Auditors need to know which model version and which features produced each transaction score. That evidence must remain associated with the individual score for later review.

alternatives.label: Persist model version and scoring features per score
pros: Audit explainability: each score has its model and features
Reproducibility: scoring inputs can be reviewed later
cons: Low latency: persistence adds work to the request path

alternatives.label: Persist scores and model version only
pros: Low latency: stores less data per score
cons: Audit explainability: cannot establish which features produced a score
Reproducibility: original scoring inputs are missing

chosen.label: Persist model version and scoring features per score

decisions.rationale: Audit explainability decides the choice because the brief specifically requires the features behind each score. This costs additional storage and request-path work.
consequences: Each score record includes its model version and feature values.
Storage and write volume grow with transaction volume.
